issues.note: Look for means try to find, not find in a source; belongs under compare.
Long gap is typical, not required; 'especially' would fix it. Minor narrowing.
American stress wrongly on look; particle carries main stress.
Example naturally implies infrequent contact; fits the visit sense.
Same wrong synonym, contradicting the learner-error note.
American IPA contradicts the note and the British IPA.
Visit sense is widely unlabeled; neutral enough, so this is taste.
Pronoun-placement fact repeated from learner errors; one fact, one field.
Largely restates senses, but does name the unrelated get-better sense.
Listed unseparated inflection needs no hand mark; not an exception case.
Sentence is grammatical, but learners do misuse look for this way.

findings.F1: look-for-phrv wrongly listed as a synonym of look up (find information); it is a confusable word for compare.
findings.F2: American IPA puts main stress on look (ˈlʊk ˌʌp), against the particle-stress convention, the British IPA, and the note.
findings.F3: The adaptation grammar note restates the pronoun-placement fact already given in learner_errors.
findings.F4: An unseparated, listed inflection in a sense 4 example carries an unnecessary hand mark.
